hook: The Casebolt House, an Article 10 individual landmark built for the blacksmith and street car manufacturer Henry Casebolt.

parcel.year_built_note: As the 2025 secured roll and SF Planning both record it. The Daily Alta California reported the house nearly completed in March 1868; see historical_record.

historic_status.reason: Article 10 Individual Landmark, California Register Historic District, Historic Survey Result

historic_district.name: Pacific Heights Historic District
historic_district.note: The district is California Register–eligible, not listed, and is not an Article 10 district; the parcel's local landmark protection comes from its own individual designation.

permits.description: cabinets and fixtures removed from one kitchen and two bathrooms, in response to a complaint; the structural work had been done under the 2009 permit
four tiebacks installed as emergency shoring
brick retaining walls on both sides of the property repaired
old shower tiles torn out and new ceramic tiles laid

permits_note: Three $1 street-space permits, a $1 filing made to obtain final inspection on the 2009 retaining-wall work, and a 1996 renewal of the 1995 tiling permit are omitted.

historical_record.description: The Daily Alta California reported Henry Casebolt's house on Pierce Street nearly completed.
A house here served as the St. Alexander Nevsky Orthodox chapel from 1874 to 1881, between Vallejo Street and what later became Green Street.

narrative.lead: Henry Casebolt, a blacksmith who became a carriage and street car manufacturer and later controlled the Sutter Street Railroad, built this house and owned the whole block bounded by Pierce, Vallejo, Scott and Green Streets.
